normalization.overview: Kirgis and coauthors report two selected shadow evaluations of research agents, covering LLM personas and TabPFN distribution shift.
normalization.whyItMatters: Worth studying if you evaluate autonomous research. Skip it as a universal forecast or a matched human comparison.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Separate research engineering from research judgment. Require expert critique and a reason to revise the method before accepting a claimed advance.
normalization.falsification: Revisit this call with blinded, broader and resource-matched evaluations, independent reproduction, full trajectory inspection or a counterexample on the same research questions.
normalization.freshness: Version-pinned paper, separate context sources and public artifact index checked 2026-10-19. Authors’ study findings remain attributed, not independently reproduced.

claims.proposition: The authors evaluated agents on two selected research questions, LLM personas and TabPFN distribution shift, with original authors grading the outputs.
claims.assessment: The study describes these two shadow questions and reviewer roles.
claims.limits: The sample is selected and grading is non-blind.

claims.proposition: Main runs had a 120-hour initial deadline and a 24-hour extension, with a harness fix and requested prose rewrite as human interventions.
claims.assessment: This is the paper authors’ reported time window and intervention account.
claims.limits: Figure pixels and underlying run logs were not independently audited.

claims.proposition: The original authors scored the Personas paper 2 of 6 and the TabPFN paper 1 of 6, while reporting substantial research engineering by the agents.
claims.assessment: The authors report completed engineering work and rejected research conclusions.
claims.limits: The scores are non-blind expert judgments, not a matched human performance result.

claims.proposition: The authors describe weak research judgment, limited response to critique, poor backtracking, resource awareness problems and instruction drift in these runs.
claims.assessment: These are the authors’ qualitative interpretations of the observed trajectories.
claims.limits: Full trajectory logs and experiments were not independently audited; causes remain open.

claims.proposition: A second model and native scaffold showed similar failure patterns on one of the two questions.
claims.assessment: This reported check bears on one scaffold-only explanation.
claims.limits: One-question check does not establish a universal model or task limit.

claims.proposition: RE-Bench and AI Scientist-v2 report agent capability in different research evaluation setups.
claims.assessment: Both are useful counterweights when interpreting a two-case study.
claims.limits: Neither replicates these shadow questions or measures the same research-progress construct.

claims.proposition: Public Personas materials exist, while the study says detailed TabPFN agent logs and paper are withheld.
claims.assessment: A public code repository supports availability of Personas materials, not experiment validation.
claims.limits: The withheld TabPFN record and full logs were not independently inspected.

evidenceReview.sourceFidelity: Study design, scores and limits checked in bounded original sections and partial private PDF/HTML anchors.
evidenceReview.conclusion: Two selected runs show substantial engineering and poor original-author ratings for the research conclusions; no universal ceiling follows.
evidenceReview.evidenceBoundary: Study-author reports remain unverified independently; RE-Bench and AI Scientist-v2 examine different constructs.
evidenceReview.nextVerification: Broader blind, resource-matched evaluation and independent experiment/log review would sharpen the claim.
